officialTitle: Gemcitabine with or without ramucirumab as second-line treatment for malignant pleural mesothelioma (RAMES): a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 2 trial

design.sampleSizeSourceQuote: Between Dec 22, 2016, and July 30, 2018, of 165 patients enrolled 161 were correctly assigned and received either gemcitabine plus placebo (n=81) or gemcitabine plus ramucirumab (n=80).
design.notes: Randomised phase 2 at 26 hospitals in Italy; efficacy reported with 70% confidence intervals per the phase 2 design.

clinicalQuestion: Does adding ramucirumab to gemcitabine improve overall survival as second-line therapy for pleural mesothelioma?

pico.population: Pleural mesothelioma progressing during or after first-line pemetrexed plus platinum, ECOG PS 0-2

arms.label: Gemcitabine + ramucirumab
arms.dosing: Gemcitabine 1000 mg/m2 days 1 and 8 every 3 weeks plus ramucirumab 10 mg/kg day 1 every 3 weeks
arms.doseSourceQuote: Patients were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive intravenous gemcitabine 1000 mg/mon days 1 and 8 every 3 weeks plus either intravenous placebo (gemcitabine plus placebo group) or ramucirumab 10 mg/kg (gemcitabine plus ramucirumab group) on day 1 every 3 weeks, until tumour progression or unacceptable toxicity.

publications.title: Gemcitabine with or without ramucirumab as second-line treatment for malignant pleural mesothelioma (RAMES): a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 2 trial.
publications.label: Primary analysis

outcomes.population: Correctly randomised patients who received allocated treatment
outcomes.sourceQuote: At database lock (March 8, 2020), with a median follow-up of 21·9 months (IQR 17·7-28·5), overall survival was longer in the ramucirumab group (HR 0·71, 70% CI 0·59-0·85; p=0·028). Median overall survival was 13·8 months (70% CI 12·7-14·4) in the gemcitabine plus ramucirumab group and 7·5 months (6·9-8·9) in the gemcitabine plus placebo group.

safety.sourceQuote: Grade 3-4 treatment-related adverse events were reported in 35 (44%) of 80 patients in the gemcitabine plus ramucirumab group and 24 (30%) of 81 in the gemcitabine plus placebo group.

limitations: Phase II with 70% confidence intervals; requires phase III confirmation
Patients were largely immunotherapy-naive, limiting relevance after first-line immunotherapy

clinicalImplications.text: Randomised phase II data suggest ramucirumab added to gemcitabine prolongs survival in second-line pleural mesothelioma; the 70% confidence intervals and phase II design mean the evidence is supportive rather than definitive.

tumourBoardPearl.text: Note the 70% confidence interval: this is a phase II signal, not phase III proof.

curation.notes: All numbers transcribed from the PubMed abstract of PMID 34499874. RAMES included as the requested alternative randomised trial alongside IND.227.
